name: google/books
description: Search Google Books by keyword and get titles, authors, snippets, publication info and preview links.

q.description: Parameter defines the query you want to search. You can use anything that you would use in a regular Google Books search: a title, an author, a subject, or a quote. Search operators such as `intitle:`, `inauthor:`, `inpublisher:`, `subject:`, and `isbn:` are supported (e.g., `inauthor:"Stephen King"`).

gl.description: Parameter defines the country to use for the Google Books search. It's a two-letter country code. (e.g., `us` for the United States, `uk` for United Kingdom, or `fr` for France). It defaults to `us`. Head to the Google countries page for a full list of supported Google countries.

hl.description: Parameter defines the language to use for the Google Books search. It's a two-letter language code. (e.g., `en` for English, `es` for Spanish, or `fr` for French). It defaults to `en`. Head to the Google languages page for a full list of supported Google languages.

tbs.description: (to be searched) parameter defines advanced search parameters that aren't possible in the regular query field. `view`, `document_type`, `start_date`, and `end_date` override the corresponding components (e.g., `bkt:s` for newspapers).

nfpr.description: Parameter defines the exclusion of results from an auto-corrected query when the original query is spelled wrong. It can be set to `1` to exclude these results, or `0` to include them (default). Note that this parameter may not prevent Google from returning results for an auto-corrected query if no other results are available.

view.description: Parameter defines how much of the books must be viewable on Google Books. It defaults to any view. Available options: `preview` - Preview and full view `full` - Full view

start.description: Parameter defines the result offset. It skips the given number of results. It's used for pagination. (e.g., `0` (default) is the first page of results, `10` is the 2nd page of results, `20` is the 3rd page of results, etc.).

device.description: Parameter defines the device to use to get the results. It can be set to `desktop` (default) to use a regular browser, `tablet` to use a tablet browser (currently using iPads), or `mobile` to use a mobile browser.

end_date.description: Parameter defines the latest publication date of the results. The format is `YYYYMMDD` (e.g., `19690731`). This parameter overrides `cdr` and `cd_max` components of `tbs` parameter.

start_date.description: Parameter defines the earliest publication date of the results. The format is `YYYYMMDD` (e.g., `19690701`). This parameter overrides `cdr` and `cd_min` components of `tbs` parameter.

document_type.description: Parameter defines the type of documents to search. It defaults to any document. Available options: `books` - Books `magazines` - Magazines `newspapers` - Newspapers Newspapers are the scanned newspapers of the Google News Archive.

google_domain.description: Parameter defines the Google domain to use. It defaults to `google.com`. Head to the Google domains page for a full list of supported Google domains.

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.

# Google Books

Search Google Books by keyword and get titles, authors, snippets, publication info and preview links.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/google/books" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"q": "machine learning"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data` as structured JSON.
